Summary:

Data-source overview:
The reference list belongs to the ICML-2018 paper “Obfuscated Gradients Give a False Sense of Security: Circumventing Defenses to Adversarial Examples”.  The paper analyses why many published defenses against adversarial examples fail, shows how new attack techniques defeat them, and recommends principled evaluation and alternative defenses (adversarial training and provable robustness).

Inference strategy justification:
Because only the bibliography is provided, I reconstructed the core reasoning chain from the well-known contents of the Athalye-et-al. paper (plus the key follow-up works it cites).  This constitutes “moderate inference”; all such edges are given confidence 1–2 and their rationales mark the inference.  The resulting fabric captures every causal path from the main risk (adversarial exploitation) through problem analyses, theoretical insights, design rationales, implementation mechanisms, validation evidence and, finally, actionable interventions.

Extraction completeness explanation:
The fabric contains 16 nodes (≈15/5 000 words guideline) and 18 edges, all mutually connected and ending in three distinct interventions (evaluation suite, certified robustness, ensemble adversarial training), thereby covering all major solution families discussed in the source.

Key limitations:
• Lack of the paper’s exact section titles forced generic references (“Main Text”, “Results”).
• Quantitative details (attack success rates, bound values) are summarised, not reproduced.
• Additional niche defenses (e.g. thermometer encoding) are omitted for brevity.
